knowledge_points.content: The inverted device architecture used for the organic solar cells is ITO / ZnO (30 nm) / PFN (5 nm) / PTB7-Th:Acceptor / MoO3 (10 nm) / Ag (70 nm).
knowledge_points.evidence: The device structure was ITO / ZnO / PFN / PTB7-Th: Acceptor / MoO3 / Ag. ... The ZnO precursor solution was spin-coated on the ITO-coated glass to form a 30 nm electron-transport layer. ... a thin layer of PFN (5nm) was spin-coated on top of the ZnO layer.

knowledge_points.content: PTB7-Th:PC71BM active layers are processed using a mixed solvent of 97% Chlorobenzene (CB) and 3% 1,8-Diiodooctane (DIO) at a concentration of 25 mg/ml.
knowledge_points.evidence: PTB7-Th: PC71BM blend was dissolved into a mixed solvent containing 97% Chlorobenzene (CB) and 3% 1,8-Diiodooctane (DIO) with a concentration of 25 mg/ml.

knowledge_points.content: In the tail state-mediated recombination model, the ideality factor (nid,t) is determined by the characteristic energy of the tail states (Et) according to the relation nid,t = 2Et / (Et + kBT).
knowledge_points.evidence: Therefore, the ideality factor nid,t can be expressed as nid,t = (kBT / 2Et + 1/2)^-1 ... nid,t = 2Et / (Et + kBT)

knowledge_points.content: For organic solar cells with carrier mobility lower than 10^-1 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1, the fill factor (FF) typically shows a negative dependence on light intensity due to transport resistance.
knowledge_points.evidence: For low mobility (< 10^-1 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1), FF becomes negatively dependent on light intensity. This result can be rationalized using an increased transport resistance in the diode equation.

knowledge_points.content: The open-circuit voltage (Voc) in a system dominated by tail state-mediated recombination is expressed as Voc = Eg/q - (nid,t * kT / q) * ln(Bt * Nt * Nc / (CG * I)).
knowledge_points.evidence: The Voc can then be written as ... Voc = Eg/q - (nid,t * kT / q) * ln(Bt * Nt * Nc / (CG * I))

knowledge_points.content: The dark ideality factor (nid,d) is extracted from the exponential regime of dark J-V curves at voltages below the onset of the Ohmic regime to eliminate series resistance effects.
knowledge_points.evidence: Therefore, to avoid influence from series resistive effect, the dark ideality factor nid,d can only be obtained by fitting the exponential regime of the dark current-voltage curves at voltages below the onset of the Ohmic regime.

knowledge_points.content: Drift-diffusion modeling using gpvdm confirms that the voltage at the maximum power point (Vm) is linearly proportional to the open-circuit voltage (Voc) for light intensities ranging from 10^-8 to 1 Sun.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S8 shows that the assumption that Vm ∝ Voc is reliable for the light intensity dependent analysis for devices limited by either direct or tail state mediated recombination. ... light intensity, which was changed from 10^-8 Suns to 1 Sun.

knowledge_points.content: Contact injection barriers at the cathode reduce the absolute fill factor but do not create a positive FF-light intensity dependence in either trap-free or trap-active organic solar cells.
knowledge_points.evidence: Therefore, the presence of contact barriers cannot contribute to a positive FF-I dependence. ... the introduction of contact injection barrier reduces FF at each light intensity, however, the same FF-I trend, i.e. negative dependency, is maintained.

knowledge_points.content: The light ideality factor (nid,l) is derived from the slope of the Voc versus the natural logarithm of light intensity (I) plot.
knowledge_points.evidence: The light ideality factor nid,l can then be obtained by fitting the Voc-Sun plot. ... Voc = nid,l * (kBT/q) * ln(I) + C2

knowledge_points.content: A positive dependence of fill factor (FF) on light intensity is an indicator that the device performance is limited by trap-involved recombination rather than direct recombination.
knowledge_points.evidence: Fig. S9b shows that the positive dependence of FF on light intensity is only present when traps are involved.

knowledge_points.content: The internal voltage at the maximum power point (Vint,m) is defined as the difference between the built-in voltage (Vbi) and the voltage at maximum power point (Vm).
knowledge_points.evidence: the internal voltage at MPP, Vint,m is given by Vint,m = Vbi - Vm

knowledge_points.content: In the tail state-mediated model, the charge transport mechanism is assumed to be drift-dominated, and the mobility is treated as a function of both free and trapped charge carrier densities.
